# Halls: working and ceremonial configurations

**Living research brief, 2026-09-22.** Start with two configurations sharing a timber support vocabulary. A smaller working hall and a monumental ceremonial hall should not be generated by scaling one arrangement uniformly.

## Inspected evidence

Sajeongjeon's retained drawings connect a five-by-three perimeter grid, inner posts, a timber floor, a roof-support assembly and a northern interior frame. Its official description identifies an internally unpartitioned space without ondol, with 우물마루, 다포 framing and a coffered ceiling beneath a double-eaved hip-and-gable roof. Its neighbouring working buildings, Manchunjeon and Cheonchujeon, have ondol. The source suggests seasonal use; that interpretation does not make absence of ondol a rule for working halls. See [drawing observations](../buildings/gbg-sajeongjeon.json) and [official description, notes 001–003](../sources/src-khs-sajeongjeon-description/source.json).

For a ceremonial configuration, Guo's study of Geunjeongjeon and Injeongjeon describes a tall single interior beneath the exterior's two-tier appearance. Its Geunjeongjeon section distinguishes inner and outer support networks. This gives a useful structural contrast with Sajeongjeon, but the article's historical attribution still needs primary survey confirmation. See [Guo 2005, note-001](../sources/src-guo-joseon-timber-2005/source.json), PDF pages 6–7, printed 55–56. Do not create an occupied upper floor merely because a roof has two tiers.

The surveyed and repair Sajeongjeon dimensions remain separate. The repair plan's more regular grid is not a correction of the unequal survey chains. Its metric interpretation helps frame an initial model, provided the model records that choice explicitly; see the [dimensional reading guide](../buildings/gbg-sajeongjeon-dimensions.md).

## Provisional fallback proposals

A **working-hall configuration** can begin with a complete post-and-beam frame, a main timber-floor interior, perimeter openings, a resolved ceiling and roof, and a platform with usable access. Furnishing and inserted display assemblies should remain separately dated. Choosing a Sajeongjeon-like arrangement without ondol is a scoped fallback, not the definition of 편전.

A **ceremonial-hall configuration** should preserve the relationship between a large interior, its inner/outer supports, the enclosing boundary and roof tiers. Keep ritual platforms, circulation and display positions explicit when the commission needs them. Proposed proportions, roof-member sizes and unresolved joints belong in the modeling brief until supported by a selected example. Neither configuration may omit necessary structure or enclosure because measurements are unavailable.

## Next useful evidence

For Sajeongjeon, resolve floor/ceiling datums and opening operation using the retained sections and remaining opening sheets. For the ceremonial configuration, inspect one primary measured section and plan for Geunjeongjeon before extracting reusable dimensions. The present brief supplies relationships, not verified load-bearing design, numeric defaults or an adopted component family.
